item.title: What changes on 1 November
item.description: From 1 November the evening suburban pair, 6005 and 6006, will leave forty minutes earlier. The dispatchers have known since August. The departure yard at Nurzhan will be under track renewal from the 3rd to the 14th, so for those days a lot of shunting will be moved to the siding. The Sary-Bulak…

item.title: The line to the outside
item.description: Since the end of June my blog is open again from outside the country. For almost three years nobody abroad could read it. I do not know who else was reading. Dima, from Siberia, wrote that he read a whole year of notes in one night. A railway is also a line to the outside. The north line to the…

item.title: Repair day
item.description: Tuesday: the 2TE10 in the depot had its turbocharger replaced by two mechanics and a cousin with a chain hoist. It took four hours. They drank tea on the engine's roof while it cooled. The foreman signed the form without reading it. I think that's what trust looks like. See Fewer than twenty.

item.title: Lugovoy
item.description: Lugovoy is a small station on the Chu line with a stationmaster, a kiosk, a bench, two switches and a well. In spring the stationmaster plants tulips on the embankment, a hundred and some, in rows, and the drivers of the passing trains slow down in May to see them. This is not in any instruction,…

item.title: A good dispatcher is boring
item.description: The job is done well when nothing happens. No delays, no stones in the river, no phone calls at four in the morning. Passengers do not know your name. If they do, something went wrong. My father is a plumber and says it is the same trade. If you hear of him, the house has flooded. See What a…

item.title: Talas North Terminal
item.description: West of Aulie-Ata the Kara-Buura line runs 145 kilometres to Talas North Terminal on the Kazakh frontier. The exchange of freight is from 08:00 to 20:00, no night work. The terminal is quiet, with a customs shed, a low yard and a long fence, and one old locomotive painted green that the border…

item.title: Lines of the north
item.description: The north line runs from Nurzhan across the eastern Chu plain to the frontier. It is the old Turksib: the line to Almaty and Siberia. At the border station the Iradi crew uncouples and a Kazakh crew couples, with a short ceremony of paper: the wagon list, the seals, the stamps. Around the clock.…

item.title: Lines of Irad: a map in words
item.description: Chu line, 229 km. Kara-Buura line, 145. Talas branch, 100. North line (Tündük linyasy), 129, to the Nurzhan rail border station where the trains are handed over to Kazakhstan and the road to Otar and Almaty. East line, 43, to Boz-Korgon. Sary-Bulak spur, 39. item.title: Reading a timetable
item.description: The printed timetable of Irad Temir Jolu has two numbers for each station: arrival and departure. Where they are the same, the train does not stop. item.title: Cold start
item.description: At minus 25 a diesel is never switched off. In the depot a locomotive will idle all night, to keep the oil and the coolant from freezing, and the fuel bill for those nights is higher than a month of summer.
